fire: Anxiety was higher among renters (Study 1) and among commuters (Study 2).
Memory improved at the group level (Experiment 1) and at the individual level (Experiment 2).
Trust declined in urban samples (Study 1) but not in rural samples (Study 2).
Reading speed improved for novices (Experiment 1) and for experts (Experiment 2).
Loneliness predicted poor sleep in students (Study 1) and in retirees (Study 2).
Participants preferred the cheaper option online (Experiment 1) and in stores (Experiment 2).
We found the same bias in nurses (Sample 1) and in teachers (Sample 2).
Attention was measured in the laboratory (Study 1) and in the field (Study 2).
quiet: Anxiety was higher among commuters in the two surveys we ran.
Memory improved at both levels in the later of our experiments.
Trust declined in urban samples but held steady across rural towns.
Reading speed improved for experts, as the follow-up (Experiment 3) showed.
Loneliness predicted poor sleep in retirees (Study 3).
Participants preferred the cheaper option online and in stores alike.
The figures for nurses and teachers appear in the appendix (Table 1).
Attention was measured in the laboratory and again in the field.
